title: Negative information questions with singular olla forms
focus: In an ordinary negative information question, keep the question word first and use the negative verb: Miksi sinä et ole kotona? Miksi sinä et ole kotona? — Koska olen koulussa.
targetSkills: Negative information questions with singular olla forms

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Why aren't you at home?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. In an ordinary negative information question, keep the question word first and use the negative verb: Miksi sinä et ole kotona? (“Why aren't you at home?”). Singular forms are minä en ole, sinä et ole and hän ei ole. Ole stays unchanged after the negative verb. The complete question means “Why aren't you at home”.
requiredSkills: Negative information questions with singular olla forms
exercises.targetSkill: Negative information questions with singular olla forms

exercises.prompt: Answer “Missä sinä et ole?”: choose “I am not at school.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. The answer supplies the requested information. A negative question does not require a negative answer: Miksi et ole kotona? can receive Koska olen koulussa (“Because I am at school”). When confirming an excluded place in a bounded comparison, En ole koulussa means I am not at school. Read the intended reply before choosing its form. The complete reply means “I am not at school”.
